top_signals.title: US Inflation Softens Ahead of Fed Data, Jackson Hole
top_signals.summary: Senior Research Economist Sree Kochugovindan from Aberdeen discussed the recent US inflation data, describing it as a subdued core inflation print that has somewhat eased pressure on the Federal Reserve. Despite inflation remaining elevated and outpacing wage growth, the inflation report was considered a bit of a nonevent. Kochugovindan emphasized that there is still more economic data to be released and the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium remains a critical event for gauging the Fed's next moves. He suggested that it is still too early to definitively extrapolate the Fed's September rate decision based solely on the latest inflation figures. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Commission accelerates IRIS² deployment with enhanced security and expanded satellites network
top_signals.summary: European Commission Press release Brussels, 07 Aug 2026 Today, the European Commission and the SpaceRISE consortium concluded negotiations and signed an implementation agreement to roll out IRIS², the European Union's new flagship satellite constellation. The agreement, among other things, adds 66 satellites into low Earth orbit to the programme, bringing the main constellation to 348 satellites, and moving it from planning to full-scale deployment.

top_signals.title: Solar Surpasses Wind In Global Electricity Generation For The First Time
top_signals.summary: In 2007, nearly two decades ago, I wrote an article called “The Future Is Solar.” At the time, my argument was largely based on efficiency. I had been comparing biofuels with direct solar energy and noted how much more effectively solar panels could capture the sun’s energy than crops could convert it into liquid fuel. Solar was still expensive, storage was a major challenge, and the world’s energy infrastructure was built around fossil fuels. But the direction seemed clear.
